name: Use Bed
desc: Makes the player lie down in a bed at the specified position.

writeup.p: S0A tells clients that a player went to sleep: a VarInt entity id and a BlockPos for the bed. The server sends it from EntityPlayerMP.sleepInBedAt and re-broadcasts it through EntityTrackerEntry to everyone tracking the sleeper. The client renders the sleeping pose; the matching wake-up arrives as S0BPacketAnimation type 2 (leave bed).

NetHandlerPlayClient.handleUseBed looks the entity up by id, validates the bed block, sets the sleeping position and marks the entity as sleeping. EntityTrackerEntry broadcasts S0A to tracking players when a tracked entity enters a bed, and EntityPlayerMP sends it on its own connection in sleepInBedAt.

No module in the 8 clients hooks S0A. The only non-vanilla reference is Rise 6.x NetworkAPI, which lists S0A in the script API packet whitelist so JavaScript modules can register receive handlers for it; that is framework plumbing, not module logic. Bed mechanics are absent from the 1.8 PvP servers these clients target, and a sleep pose carries no combat, movement or render value, so nothing listens.

None observed in the corpus. The packet is clientbound and informational: it changes only a render pose. The bed-position BlockPos is never validated by clients for gameplay effect, and no anti-cheat measures sleeping. The honest assessment is that S0A is protocol trivia in this ecosystem: it exists, it is registered in every client's EnumConnectionState, and nothing exploits it.

implementation.overview: The sleep-pose broadcast: entity id plus bed BlockPos, sent on join and re-broadcast by the entity tracker. Zero module hits across the 8 clients; the only non-vanilla reference is the Rise script API packet whitelist. Bed mechanics do not exist on the servers these clients target, so S0A is protocol trivia.
implementation.server_handling: EntityPlayerMP.sleepInBedAt constructs S0A with the player and bed location and sends it on the sleeper's own connection; EntityTrackerEntry re-broadcasts it to all tracking players. There is no server-side validation of the pose beyond the bed-block checks in the sleep routine itself.
implementation.protocol_notes: Fields: VarInt entity id, then BlockPos serialized as a long (x << 38 | z << 12 | y, with the y sign bit). Sent in PLAY state, clientbound. The leave-bed counterpart is S0BPacketAnimation type 2, so the two packets bracket a sleep cycle. Registered at id 0x0A in every client's EnumConnectionState.
implementation.anticheat_landscape: Nothing to flag: S0A changes only a pose and carries no timing, position or state information an anti-cheat could measure. The only ecosystem wrinkle is that a client which never renders the sleep pose (or renders it wrong) produces a visual mismatch, never a flag.
implementation.general_hooks: Rise 6.x scripts can register S0A receive handlers through NetworkAPI, but no shipped module does.
implementation.client_variations: All 8 clients register S0A in vanilla code paths identically; only Rise 6.x adds the script API whitelist entry.
